chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jamilah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who performs sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah without wudu (ablution), so he said: There is no harm.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Safa, one of the two well-known sites of sa'y in hajj and 'umrah
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other site between which sa'y is performed
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible and unobjectionable
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before certain acts of worship
key_terms.يَسْعَى: he performs sa'y, meaning he traverses ritually between al-Safa and al-Marwah

ai.seo_question: Is wudu (ablution) required for sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah during hajj or 'umrah. It indicates that performing sa'y without wudu (ablution) is permissible and does not invalidate the act.
